extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent practitioners/applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and examiner guidance for handling applications and reexamination proceedings after decisions by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, including withdrawals, dismissals, reopening prosecution, RCEs, amendments after decision, and judicial review timing/choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when Board affirms some claims and reverses others
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board affirms a rejection against independent claim(s) and reverses rejections against dependent claim(s) thereby leaving other claim(s) allowed, the examiner should either convert the dependent claim into independent form by examiner’s amendment and cancel the affirmed independent claim(s) and issue the application with the resulting claims, or set a ONE MONTH time limit for appellant to rewrite the dependent claim(s) in independent form (no extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) permitted). If no timely reply is received, cancel the affirmed independent claim(s) and any dependent claims not rewritten, and issue on the allowed claim(s) only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two explicit options (A or B). If option B used, NO EXTENSIONS OF TIME UNDER 37 CFR 1.136(a) WILL BE GRANTED. Use form paragraph language (¶12.119.*) to notify applicant. If uncorrected formal matters remain that cannot be handled without correspondence, take appropriate action on those formal matters but otherwise close prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph ¶12.119.01 / ¶12.119.02 for sustained-in-part decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard form paragraphs to inform applicant when the Board affirmed rejection(s) against independent claim(s) but reversed rejections against dependent claim(s), and to set the ONE MONTH period for presenting dependent claims in independent form (or to notify of lack of an allowed claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inserts bracketed items: bracket 1 = independent claim number(s) for which Board affirmed; bracket 2 = dependent claim number(s) for which Board reversed; bracket 3 = allowed claim numbers (if any). Emphasize ONE MONTH time period and NO EXTENSIONS under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (where applicable). Prosecution otherwise closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for seeking court review has lapsed (form ¶12.120)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the period under 37 CFR 1.304 for seeking court review has expired and appellant took no further action, the proceedings as to rejected claims are terminated; the application will be passed to issue on allowed claims provided formal matters are promptly corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must correct formal matters within a shortened statutory period set to expire ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date to avoid ABANDONMENT. Extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136. Use ¶12.120 to notify applicant and list the formal matters (bracket 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims require action when affirmance-in-part brings claims up on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board's partially affirming decision reverses a rejection that brings certain claims up for action on the merits (e.g., generic claims or nonelected species), the examiner will take up the application or reexamination for appropriate action on the matters thus brought up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application/proceeding remains closed to further prosecution except as to the specific matters brought up by the Board’s reversal. Handle only those matters; do not open general prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of new rejections under 37 CFR 41.50(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board makes a new rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) and appellant takes no action within two months, the examiner should proceed as indicated in the relevant MPEP paragraphs (I–III).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1214.01 for detailed procedures. The two-month period is important; absence of appellant action triggers examiner follow-up per the referenced paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when Board affirms examiner rejection but enters new ground under 41.50(b) – appellant proceeds before examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board affirms the examiner’s rejection but also enters a new ground under 37 CFR 41.50(b) and the appellant elects to proceed before the examiner with regard to the new rejection, the Board’s affirmance will be treated as nonfinal and no rehearing of the affirmance need be filed at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution before the examiner of the 41.50(b) rejection can incidentally overcome the affirmed rejection even though that affirmed rejection is not open to further prosecution. If application becomes allowed during limited prosecution, do not return it to the Board. If not overcome, applicant may file a second appeal limited to the 41.50(b) rejection (may not include the affirmed rejection). If prosecution of the 41.50(b) claims terminates before the examiner without allowance/abandonment, return the file to the Board so the original affirmance can be made final. Similar rules apply in ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when appellant requests rehearing of a new 41.50(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant elects to request rehearing of the new rejection (and of the affirmance), the request for rehearing must be filed within two months from the date of the Board’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness (two months) is mandatory for requesting rehearing of both the new rejection and the affirmance as provided in MPEP §1214.01 paragraph II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after final Board decision (37 CFR 1.198)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Board decision has become final for judicial review, prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened or reconsidered except under 37 CFR 1.114 (RCE) or 37 CFR 41.50 and only with the Director’s written authority and for matters not already adjudicated with sufficient cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to reopen under 1.198 are exceptional. Do not reopen prosecution as a matter of routine once the decision is final for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after Board decision: entry and RCE practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the Board’s decision that does not implement a Board suggestion and that presents new/amended claims is not entitled to be entered as a matter of right because prosecution is closed. However, if submitted with a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 and the required fee, prosecution will be reopened and the amendment entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant patents filed before June 8, 1995, design applications, or certain reexamination proceedings (see 1.114(d) and MPEP §706.07(h)). An appeal brief or reply brief alone is not a submission under 1.114 unless the RCE transmittal letter expressly incorporates the earlier arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendment that obviously places application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment obviously places an application in condition for allowance, regardless of whether it is filed with an RCE, the primary examiner should recommend that the amendment be entered and, with supervisory concurrence, the amendment will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note MPEP §1002.02(d). Even after final Board decision, entry is appropriate when the amendment plainly puts the case in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendment cannot be entered: notice and non-arbitrary refusal (form ¶12.119)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment cannot be entered, the examiner should notify the appellant in writing indicating the reason; the refusal may not be arbitrary or capricious. Use form paragraph ¶12.119 (Amendment After Board Decision, Entry Refused) where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 of ¶12.119 insert date amendment was filed. Do not use ¶12.119 where a 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejection has been made by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 decided by Technology Center Director: acceptance categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to reopen or reconsider prosecution after a Board decision (with no court action) are decided by the Technology Center Director (MPEP §1002.02(c)). The Director will ordinarily entertain petitions only in these categories: (A) Board decision suggests claim limitation or cure would lead to allowability; (B) Board decision indicates record lacks evidence of specified character and such evidence exists and can be offered; (C) Board decision is based on a practice, rule, law, or precedent which has since been rescinded, repealed, or overruled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions are exceptional and ordinarily not entertained after the Director’s brief has been filed in a 35 U.S.C. 141 review or after trial in a 35 U.S.C. 145 case. If granted in a 141 appeal, steps will be taken to request remand so proposed amendments/evidence are entered of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal under 37 CFR 1.34 and abandonment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney not of record may file a paper under 37 CFR 1.34 withdrawing an appeal. Except where withdrawal results in a continuing application filed the same date, withdrawal where no allowable claims appear is an express abandonment that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.138.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawal is filed after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired, the application is considered abandoned as of the date of withdrawal unless there are allowed claims in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of abandonment on filing letter of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter abandoning the application in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138 has an effective date of abandonment equal to the date of recognition of the letter by an appropriate Office official, or a different date if specified in the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §711.01. If a brief had been filed within the permitted time and an answer mailed and appellant withdraws the appeal, the application is returned to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE while an appeal is pending reopens prosecution and withdraws appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a Board decision, an applicant may withdraw an application from appeal and reopen prosecution by filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 accompanied by a submission (a reply responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last outstanding Office action) and the RCE fee; filing an RCE is treated as a withdrawal of the appeal regardless of whether the RCE includes the fee or a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to certain earlier-filed utility/plant applications or design applications or reexamination proceedings as specified. If an RCE is filed without the appropriate fee or submission in an application that has no allowed claims, the application will be considered abandoned. To avoid abandonment, comply strictly with 37 CFR 1.114 and MPEP §706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution in response to examiner’s new ground or supplemental answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a notice of appeal has been filed, appellant may request prosecution be reopened by filing: (A) a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 addressing a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer within two months from mailing of the examiner’s answer; or (B) a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 addressing a remanded rejection in a supplemental examiner’s answer within two months from mailing of the supplemental answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§1207.03 and 1207.05 for details. Timely reply under 1.111 is required to reopen prosecution in these circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify Board Chief Clerk when refiling or abandoning applications with pending appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should promptly inform the Chief Clerk of the Board in writing as soon as they decide to refile or to abandon an application containing an appeal awaiting a decision, and should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in such an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to exercise diligence may result in the Board refusing an otherwise proper request to vacate its decision. Prompt communication avoids procedural complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal of appeal on applications with no allowed claims (examples of examiner actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon withdrawal of the appeal, an application having no allowed claims will be abandoned. Examiner should act as shown in examples: (A) If claim 1 is allowed and claims 2 and 3 are rejected -> cancel claims 2 and 3 and issue on claim 1 only. (B) If claims 1–3 are rejected -> hold application abandoned. (C) If claim 1 is rejected and claim 2 objected as allowable only because dependent on claim 1 -> hold application abandoned. (D) If claim 1 rejected, claim 2 allowable only due to dependency, and independent claim 3 allowed -> cancel claims 1 and 2 and issue on claim 3 only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate consistent examiner disposition depending on which claims stand allowed when an appeal is withdrawn. In ex parte reexamination, issue an ex parte reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims standing allowed: withdrawal does not abandon application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains allowed claims as well as claims on appeal, withdrawal of the appeal does not operate as abandonment of the application; it is considered a withdrawal of the appeal as to those claims and authorizes the examiner to cancel them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment cancelling the appealed claims is equivalent to a withdrawal of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial withdrawal of appeal as to some claims (¶12.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawal of the appeal as to some claims operates as authorization to cancel those claims from the application or reexamination proceeding; the appeal continues as to remaining claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should cancel the withdrawn claims at the time of the partial withdrawal and may use form paragraph ¶12.121 to notify the applicant. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to new ground(s) in examiner’s answer -> sua sponte dismissal (¶12.179.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to file either a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing new ground(s) of rejection contained in an examiner’s answer within two months of the mailing of the examiner’s answer, the appeal is sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the new ground(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph ¶12.179.02 to notify appellant, inserting mailing date(s) and claim numbers in the brackets. Only remaining claims not subject to the new ground continue on appeal and the file is forwarded to the Board after mailing the communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to supplemental examiner’s answer remand -> sua sponte dismissal (¶12.186)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief within two months from the mailing of a supplemental examiner’s answer written in response to a Board remand (37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)), the appeal is sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to that remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph ¶12.186 to notify appellant, inserting mailing date(s) and claim numbers in the brackets. The application will be forwarded to the Board after mailing of the communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeal for failure to file brief within 37 CFR 41.37 time
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule. PTOL-461 notifying appellant that the appeal stands dismissed is not an action and does not start any period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no claims stand allowed, the application is considered abandoned on the date the brief was due. If claims stand allowed, failure to file the brief and consequent dismissal is treated as a withdrawal of the appeal for non-allowed claims and the application should be passed to issue. Do not dismiss until the extended period (up to five months under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file the brief has expired, unless appellant specifically withdraws the appeal as to rejected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling remaining formal matters when appeal dismissed but formal corrections required (¶12.109.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If formal matters remain to be attended to after dismissal or conversion to allowance, the examiner should handle the formal matters (e.g., by examiner’s amendment) or use form paragraph ¶12.109.01 to describe the formal matters required to be corrected and set a shortened period for reply. Prosecution is otherwise closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶12.109.01 should only be used if the formal matters cannot be handled by examiner’s amendment. Require correction within a shortened statutory period (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) to avoid abandonment. Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to reply to notice of noncompliance with 41.37(d) and petitions to revive/reinstate
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal will be dismissed if applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance with 37 CFR 41.37(d). If no allowed claims remain the application is abandoned as of the date the reply was due. Applicant may petition to revive and to reinstate the appeal; if allowed claims remain and some claims were cancelled by dismissal, a petition with a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 is required to reinstate the canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper reply to the notice of noncompliance must be filed before a petition to reinstate will be considered on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing notice of appeal or civil action (37 CFR 1.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or for commencing a civil action is two months from the date of the Board’s decision. If a request for rehearing is filed within the time provided, the time for filing an appeal or civil action runs two months after action on the request. Cross-appeal timing rules also apply (14 days after service or two months after decision, whichever is later for contested cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time periods set forth are not subject to 37 CFR 1.136 (extensions), 1.550(c), 1.956, or 41.4. Director may extend time for good cause if requested in writing before expiration, or after expiration on showing of excusable neglect. Days are calendar days; months are calendar months; special rule for February 28 and weekends/holidays (add one day or extend to next business day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of judicial review routes and waiver consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a Board decision may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141) or commence a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145; by filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit the applicant waives the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145. For ex parte reexaminations filed before Nov. 29, 1999 the patent owner may appeal to either the Federal Circuit (141) or bring a civil action (145); for reexaminations filed on/after Nov. 29, 1999, appeal is only to the Federal Circuit (141). Inter partes reexamination judicial review is governed by 35 U.S.C. 315.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of differing rules based on filing dates of reexamination and the consequences of electing an appeal route (waiver of 145). See 37 CFR 1.301–1.303 for procedural steps (notice of appeal filing, fees, service).
